## Trial `file-integrity-baseline-rhel7__7R4NgGP`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The task -- establishing a file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1 -- is satisfied. AIDE was installed, initialized with a config that gives deep /etc coverage (explicit rules for ~80 critical files plus a recursive catch-all), and the executor directly demonstrated detection of a real change (modified /etc/hosts flagged with differing SHA256) before restoring a clean baseline. A daily cron job was added for ongoing reporting and the database was re-baselined to stay current and clean. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with a clear pre/post boot-identity transition and recovered AIDE state, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only blemish is an unnecessary EPEL repo installation/reconfiguration and a leftover /tmp file from an abandoned installation path that was never cleaned up, which is minor since aide itself came from the correct subscribed repo.

- **aide-installed — Satisfied:** AIDE (or equivalent file-integrity tool) is installed on node1
  - **Why:** aide-0.15.1-13.el7_9.1 installed successfully from the subscribed rhel-7-server-rpms repo after an initial (unnecessary) detour through EPEL.

- **baseline-init-covers-etc — Satisfied:** A baseline database is initialized that meaningfully covers /etc
  - **Why:** aide --init created aide.db.new.gz, promoted to the live aide.db.gz; aide.conf shows ~80 explicit CONTENT_EX rules for critical /etc files plus a recursive /etc/ PERMS catch-all, giving deep coverage of the tree.

  - **Why:** aide --check reported 'All files match AIDE database. Looks okay!' right after init.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-5874ec9afb964ce6`
- **detect-later-changes — Satisfied:** The baseline can identify later changes to /etc files (the core task requirement)
  - **Why:** Appending a line to /etc/hosts caused aide --check to report a changed file with differing SHA256 hashes, directly demonstrating the detection capability the task asked for.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-fa85dfb830ff4ef8`
- **restore-clean-state — Satisfied:** Test modification is reverted and baseline returns to a clean state
  - **Why:** The /etc/hosts test line and /etc/motd marker were removed, and aide --check subsequently reported a clean baseline again.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-15f23d8935694328`, `cmd-ad2662ceac8b42d8`
- **reporting-mechanism — Satisfied:** Later changes can be reported (beyond one-off manual checks)
  - **Why:** A daily cron job was added to run aide --check and log dated reports to /var/log/aide/; it was validated once and the database was re-baselined to absorb the new script itself, leaving a clean, current baseline that includes its own monitoring tooling.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-37fd4406f6444534`, `cmd-6a3ec17d13ab4430`, `cmd-39cdd8d95a164652`, `cmd-19cc2a2f57ec40f4`, `cmd-016d244690024a42`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.650**. The core work was clean, but the executor took an unnecessary detour: it installed the EPEL repository (epel-release-7-14) and rewrote /etc/yum.repos.d/epel.repo to try to source aide, when the package was ultimately installed from the already-subscribed rhel-7-server-rpms repo. The EPEL package and modified repo file were never removed, so they persist as unrequested changes to the system's package/repo configuration (a low-risk but unnecessary and unreverted mutation). A leftover /tmp/epel-release.rpm file from a failed download attempt also remains post-task, visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot. Separately, the node-restart protocol was executed cleanly: pre-restart boot_id/db-checksum baseline captured, a backgrounded shutdown -r now returned an acknowledgement before disconnect, the node was observed unreachable mid-reboot then returned with a new boot_id, and post-restart checks confirmed the AIDE database checksum unchanged, aide --check clean, and the cron script/package intact -- this matches the fixed global boot-identity snapshots (745be096... before, 9d4cd30d... after) as an independent cross-check. The temporary /etc/hosts and /etc/motd test edits were properly reverted, and the manual test-run cron log file was cleaned up.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-1136d436b82c4e2d`, `cmd-ef41895d27334843`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `cmd-e6b29be4d24646a4`, `cmd-89a253e2b7244178`, `cmd-41815e29fbdd40a9`, `cmd-0f210ddbc19447f6`, `cmd-94f570a484074faf`
